newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Nigerian military ruler visits Ivory Coast, Guinea.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian military ruler visits Ivory Coast, Guinea.

text.p: Nigeria's military ruler General Sani Abacha paid a brief visit to Ivory Coast on Monday for talks on the situation in Sierra Leone, before heading for Guinea for further discussions, officials said.
Abacha heads the 16-nation Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) which is trying to reverse a May 25 coup which toppled Sierra Leone's president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
Ivorian Foreign Minister Essy Amara told Reuters Abacha's visit was for consultations on the Sierra Leone situation before a full ECOWAS summit in Nigeria on August 27-29.
"We will assess if there has been any progress on the (Sierra Leone) situation at the summit and take a decision from there," Essy said.
ECOWAS says it reserves the right to resort to force if diplomacy fails to reinstate Kabbah's elected government.
Abacha was received at Abidjan airport by Ivorian President Henri Konan Bedie. They held private talks at the airport and met again later at Bedie's office in the city centre.
There was no word on the substance of their discussions.
Nigeria, Ivory Coast, Guinea and Ghana are members of a special ECOWAS seeking a peaceful resolution of the Sierra Leone crisis.
Nigeria leads the community's military wing, whose troops are confronting the coup leaders and enforcing a regional economic embargo clamped on Sierra Leone since the coup.

Kabbah is exiled in Guinea, which borders his homeland, and Abacha was expected to hold talks with the ousted leader in Conakry, as well as meet Guinean President Lansana Conteh, Ivorian officials said.
Kabbah is also expected to lead a delegation of his ousted government to the ECOWAS summit in Abuja.
The United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity have condemned the coup and demanded the reinstatement of Kabbah, who was toppled just over a year after his election.
Talks between foreign ministers of the special committee and envoys of the Freetown regime broke down last month after junta leader Johnny Paul Koroma announced he would retain power until 2001.
ECOWAS ordered sanctions to be stepped up and Nigerian troops clashed last week at Freetown airport with Sierra Leone soldiers backed by former rebels who rallied to support the coup.
